tree_state: the files listed under sha256 are uncommitted at recording time and are committed in the commit that follows this record; the recorded commit is its parent
summary: The image loader-diag-xnu-ne1-usb: NAT-065's md0 image (same loader, kernel, ADT and probe-init ramdisk) with the tag NAT067-md0 and the boot-args e1stouch=0 e1sbattery=0 appended, so that the e1s touch and battery drivers return before they map any register (NAT-066 died in _e1s_touch_init on a physical-address GPIO read). Its derived driver and analyser, 24 host tests, 36/37 mutants killed (1 equivalent), decision 0028 drafted. Nothing ran on the phone.
evidence_category: host-test (derivation by asserted text substitution, static reads of the real payload, the pinned e1s patches and the pinned kernel's Mach-O symbol table, the derived driver/analyser against temporary trees and the real NAT-066 kernel log). No android-userland and no native-device evidence.

acceptance.1_build: build.py loads NAT-065's build and replaces the image name, the nat_attempt tag and the appended boot-args; two builds (build-001, build-002) give identical hashes; the command line is NAT-065's with NAT065-md0 -> NAT067-md0 and ' e1stouch=0 e1sbattery=0' appended (227 bytes, under the 256-byte field); every input is pinned by SHA-256 (build.json nat065_pins, carried unchanged); the build refuses a command line that already has the new boot-args.
acceptance.2_tests: test_nat067.py (24 tests, 0 skipped: Build, Payload, Kernel, Package, Driver, Analyser): the loader Image differs from NAT-065's in exactly six boot-id/name immediate words, the XNU payload only in the command-line field, the ramdisk is NAT-065's; both boot-arg names are parsed by the pinned e1s patches and both drivers return at the check before mapping a register; the NAT-066 abort address lies in _e1s_touch_init in the pinned kernel's symbols; the committed driver equals derive.py's output and the derivation changes exactly seven listed lines; the gates refuse a missing/ambiguous decision file, a missing hash or 'decision 0019', native unset or citing another file, and each undone required task; the analyser reads the real NAT-066 log as other-panic and a probe exit as probe-ran-to-exit, and does not accept another image's boot.
acceptance.3_mutants: mutants.py: 37 mutants (command line, tags, pins, derivation, driver, analyser); 36 killed, 1 equivalent (D9, reason in mutants.py), none survived, none invalid.
acceptance.4_decision_draft: decision-draft.md names both hashes (RECOVERY ae946b4b..., Image.payload 9fd29fb9...), decision 0019, what the kernel may now touch beyond NAT-066 (the rest of bsd_init, load_init_program, exec of a user-mode Mach-O, scheduler and syscalls, unbounded reach), what stays unknown, the pass rule root.outcome == probe-ran-to-exit and the informative outcomes; it records no run-specific owner confirmation (standing statements of decisions 0025/0026 cited) and nothing ran on the phone; every 64-hex string in it was checked against the build/package records or the files.

established: Host-test: the image is reproducible (two builds identical) and differs from the one that ran in NAT-066 only in the six boot-id immediates of the loader and the command-line field of the XNU payload (ADT, kernel and ramdisk unchanged).
Host-test: the boot-arg names e1stouch and e1sbattery are the ones the pinned patches parse with PE_parse_boot_argn, and the early return precedes any ml_io_map or register access in both drivers.
Host-test: the NAT-066 data abort (pc 0xfffffff0074a1444) lies inside _e1s_touch_init in the pinned kernel's Mach-O symbols, and the patch reads GPIO through physical-address macros.

Host-test: the derived driver and analyser cannot be used for another image or without the decision file naming both hashes and decision 0019, and the analyser keeps the NAT-066 outcome distinct from a pass.
not_established: That e1stouch=0 e1sbattery=0 is sufficient: other drivers or services may fault later in bsd_init (nothing after _e1s_touch_init has run on this phone).

That mockfs serves the ramdisk bytes as /sbin/launchd, that exec of the ad-hoc-signed probe is permitted with cs_enforcement_disable=1 (rd=md0 skips FSIOC_KERNEL_ROOTAUTH per NAT-064's source review), that PID 1's console text reaches loader_log.
That the timed loader_return_after=8 return works (NAT-063 and NAT-066 both returned through the panic path).
findings: A same-length image name keeps the loader layout: the first attempt with a longer name moved the loader (40007 differing bytes); the same-length name differs in 14 bytes (six immediate words).
The analyser wrapper must restore the patched NAT-065 entry point in a finally block, or the wrapper calls itself.
A derived value that is identical to the base's (CANARY_LEN) is invisible to a test that feeds the real pins; the derivation test also feeds different pin values (mutant D8).
